label: selected work
heading: things that had to not break

items.name: PropertyMe
items.note: Flutter app for property owners and tenants, two audiences through one codebase. His main product for four years.

items.name: PropertyMe Agent
items.note: The mobile counterpart for property managers doing the job away from a desk — inspections, appointments, workflow the owner and tenant app doesn't carry. Shares a backend with its sibling app.

items.name: Gruntify
items.note: Android GIS platform for field workers — inspection teams and crews on site, with AR features. Several Australian local government councils are clients, alongside enterprise SaaS customers.

items.name: Ozone Warehouse
items.note: Android on industrial barcode scanners — kiosk mode, self-updating, five warehouse processes off paper. If it stopped, the warehouse stopped.

items.name: Wincanton Fire Safety
items.note: VR fire-safety training for a UK logistics company — rehearsing dangerous procedures without the danger, the most clearly justified use of VR on this list.

items.name: Ozone Transport
items.note: Android app for company drivers — daily delivery tasks, live reporting per stop, and parcel barcode scanning with the phone camera. Built in-house alongside Ozone Warehouse.

items.name: Hood VR
items.note: VR recycling game built for Romania's Ministry of National Education, presented in more than 20 schools — the widest reach of anything here.

items.name: Montblanc Hub
items.note: Companion app for Montblanc's smart writing set. Added support for a graphic tablet that was still in the hardware workshop, and moved it from A5 to A4.

items.name: Atlantic Money
items.note: Banking outside the branch — a mobile app letting a financial institution's representatives serve customers in Cameroon, where branch infrastructure doesn't reach.

items.name: OMV VR
items.note: Promotional VR game for a fuel brand, never shipped to a store — delivered instead at live events, touring the country with GearVR headsets.

items.name: Stylebox
items.note: An OpenCart store built for free, in his own time, for his mother's business — plus a companion WebView app. Went on to generate real revenue before the business closed.

items.name: Hellboy VR
items.note: Dual 8K stereoscopic video on phone-driven headsets, for Lions Gate. No active cooling, one frame budget.

items.name: MyKi
items.note: Children's smartwatch companion — and the games running on the watch itself, in Java, on a very small screen.

items.name: Mtel TV Box
items.note: Launcher for a set-top box from Mtel, Bulgaria's largest mobile operator. Remote-control navigation, ten-foot interface, not a phone.

items.name: Madara Rider AR
items.note: AR tourism proof of concept — recognises Bulgaria's Madara Rider rock relief and plays a promotional video, built with Vuforia on Unity3D. A fast technology evaluation, not delivered work.

items.name: Neonatal monitoring
items.note: Tablet app reading pulse oximeters for newborns over Bluetooth Low Energy, against firmware that changed underneath it.

items.name: Happy Call
items.note: WebView Android app providing a ringback tone service for a telecoms operator, using Firebase notifications. One of his first professional projects.
